morning.name: Red Fort
morning.description: Explore the imposing red sandstone fortress that once housed Mughal emperors, and walk the Chatta Chowk market inside its walls.

afternoon.name: Jama Masjid
afternoon.description: Climb the southern minaret of India's largest mosque for sweeping views over Old Delhi's rooftops.

afternoon.name: Chandni Chowk Food Walk
afternoon.description: Wind through the spice lanes tasting parathas, jalebis, and kebabs in one of Delhi's oldest markets.

evening.name: Raj Ghat
evening.description: Visit the peaceful memorial park dedicated to Mahatma Gandhi along the Yamuna riverbank.

night.name: Karim's Old Delhi
night.description: Close the day with legendary Mughlai kebabs and curries at this century-old eatery near Jama Masjid.

restaurants.name: Karim's
restaurants.description: Old Delhi institution serving slow-cooked kebabs and curries since 1913.

restaurants.name: Paranthe Wali Gali
restaurants.description: A narrow lane packed with stalls frying stuffed parathas in every filling imaginable.

hotel.name: Hotel Heritage Inn
hotel.description: A budget-friendly stay minutes from Chandni Chowk metro station, with rooftop views of the old city.

morning.name: Humayun's Tomb
morning.description: Wander the Persian gardens surrounding this UNESCO World Heritage tomb, a precursor to the Taj Mahal.

afternoon.name: India Gate & Rajpath
afternoon.description: Stroll along the ceremonial boulevard leading up to this 42-metre war memorial arch.

afternoon.name: National Museum
afternoon.description: Browse artefacts spanning 5,000 years of Indian history, from Harappan seals to Mughal miniatures.

evening.name: Lodhi Gardens
evening.description: Watch the sunset over 15th-century tombs scattered through this leafy park favoured by joggers and picnickers.

night.name: Khan Market Dinner
night.description: Sample modern Indian small plates at one of the capital's most popular dining strips.

restaurants.name: Sattvik
restaurants.description: Wholesome thalis and regional specialities served in a calm, contemporary space.

restaurants.name: Khan Chacha
restaurants.description: Famous kathi rolls stuffed with grilled paneer, chicken, or mutton, best eaten standing up.

hotel.name: Hotel Heritage Inn
hotel.description: Same stay as Day 1 — centrally located for easy access to both old and new Delhi.

morning.name: Akshardham Temple
morning.description: Marvel at the intricately carved sandstone-and-marble complex, one of the world's largest Hindu temples.

afternoon.name: Hauz Khas Village
afternoon.description: Explore a 13th-century madrasa and tomb ruins beside a lake, surrounded by boutiques and cafés.

evening.name: Dilli Haat
evening.description: Pick up handicrafts and textiles from every Indian state at this open-air crafts bazaar.

night.name: Farewell Street Food Trail
night.description: End the trip sampling chaat, kulfi, and lassi around Bengali Market before an early flight home.

restaurants.name: Bengali Market Chaat Corner
restaurants.description: A cluster of decades-old stalls serving Delhi's favourite chaats and golgappas.

restaurants.name: Kuremal Mohan Lal Kulfi Wale
restaurants.description: Fruit-stuffed kulfis served the traditional way, a Delhi dessert institution since 1908.

hotel.name: Hotel Heritage Inn
hotel.description: Final night stay before departure, walking distance from the metro for an easy airport transfer.

travel_tips: Carry small denomination cash — many street food stalls in Old Delhi don't accept cards.
Use the Delhi Metro to skip traffic; it's the fastest way between old and new Delhi.
Cover your head and shoulders when visiting Jama Masjid and Akshardham Temple.
Bargain gently at Dilli Haat and Chandni Chowk — it's expected and part of the experience.
Book Akshardham Temple's evening water show tickets a day in advance during peak season.
